name: King Hussein International Airport
before:
Jordan's Red Sea airport, just north of Aqaba, and one of only three civilian airports in the country alongside Queen Alia and Amman's City Airport.

The geography is remarkable. Within a 24 km radius of Aqaba there are three other countries, Egypt, Saudi Arabia and Israel, and a second airport at Ramon opened across the Israeli border in 2019 nominally serving Eilat.

Weather is rarely a problem. Conditions are normally excellent and the airport is seldom closed, though strong southerly winds can carry sandstorms across the Red Sea from Egypt. There is a single runway with a Category I instrument landing system.

It is a busier site than the passenger traffic suggests, with a cargo terminal opened in January 2005, a private jet terminal, an aircraft maintenance centre, a light aircraft assembly plant, two flying academies and a Royal Pavilion, since King Abdullah II keeps a palace on the shoreline.

One caveat. The airport was reported to have been hit in a missile attack in July 2026, with damage to aircraft on the ground, and accounts of the incident differ. Check the current operating position before committing a client.
after:
King Hussein International is Aqaba's airport, just north of the city, with a single runway.

The FCDO reports Iranian strikes on targets in Jordan since July 2026, with renewed attacks and interceptions in and around Aqaba in early September, and tells British nationals in the Middle East to be prepared for flight cancellations and airspace closures.

Check the current operating position before committing a client.
